title: Variance-Optimal State Resampling for Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards
claim: Learning signal peaks at intermediate states where outcomes are mixed, so sampling states by reachability times outcome variability beats uniform sampling.
layout: 3 columns top-to-bottom: token strip, outcome panels, bar charts, formula below
description: A token trajectory runs across the top, starting from a 'prompt' box and ending in an ellipsis. Three tokens are highlighted in teal, blue and orange, and colored arrows run from them down to three tinted panels. Each panel shows five boxes marked X or check. The teal early-prefix panel has all X (mostly fail, low signal). The blue frontier-prefix panel has mixed marks (highest signal). The orange late-prefix panel has all checks (mostly succeed, low signal). Under each panel, paired bars compare a plain white RL sampling weight with a hatched VSR+RL weight. The hatched bar is tallest for the frontier prefix and short for the other two. A formula at the bottom, μ_var(s) ∝ d^π(s) σ_π(s), is labeled 'reachability' × 'future outcome variability'. The eye goes first to the colored panels and bars.
caption: Continuations from early prefixes mostly fail and from late prefixes mostly succeed; both yield low signal. VSR samples states in proportion to dπ(s) σπ(s) to capture the highest signal.
abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards spends much of its rollout budget on states that yield no learning signal. We recast this as a question about the sampling distribution itself: under a fixed rollout budget, which distribution over states minimizes the variance of the policy-gradient estimator? The answer admits a closed-form Neyman allocation, $Î¼_{\mathrm{var}}^Ï(s) \propto d^Ï(s)\,Ï_Ï(s)$, which connects naturally to GRPO's group-relative advantage and induces an emergent reverse curriculum as the policy improves, with no externally imposed schedule. Building on this principle, we propose VSR (Variance-driven State Resampling), a plug-in modification to GRPO using a prefix replay buffer and a zero-cost variance proxy. On mathematical reasoning benchmarks and long-horizon agentic tasks (Sokoban, BabyAI), VSR outperforms GRPO and GiGPO on most benchmarks with fewer generated tokens per update.
